summary: Genuine, good-faith counter-evidence attempts were made against all 6 target claims from counter-evidence-plan.md. Findings: (1) SO-ARM100 cost claims ($115/$230) are understated — vendor listings and cross-vendor pricing put a complete single arm at ~$200-230, and two unresolved GitHub issues (one closed 'not planned') document real, ongoing calibration friction beyond vendor/press framing; the 'thousands of builders' figure remains unverifiable either way (no independent count found). (2) LeKiwi's reference/upstream BOM ($482-499, excluding 3D printing) is lower than and not cleanly reconcilable with the brief's cited $660 figure; an independent, non-affiliated builder (Foxglove blog) corroborates real buildability and reports no major friction — reported honestly as claim-supporting; independence of robotsthatexist.com/growbotics.ai as verifiers vs. aggregators could not be resolved this round because both are JS-rendered pages WebFetch cannot read and the agent-browser skill's `belt` CLI is not installed/authenticated in this environment — flagged as a genuine tooling gap, not treated as a finding either way. (3) The dynamics/Ch.8 'structural gap' claim was resolved with primary technical evidence and is substantially corroborated, not contradicted: Feetech servos do support current-based torque sensing in principle (used in an independent third-party project), but no default/documented tutorial path for these candidates uses it, and OpenCat's firmware (directly inspected) confirms precomputed gait tables with no runtime dynamics computation. (4) The Bittle/OpenCat 'genuine IK, not pre-baked motions' claim is directly contradicted by primary firmware source inspection: InstinctBittle.h stores precomputed joint-angle lookup tables; IK is computed offline via a separate community tool and baked into the tables, not solved live on-device; the brief's own cited README source doesn't currently contain the term 'inverse kinematics' at all. (5) The Bittle-currency claim is qualified by the current official README's own statement that the original 2020-era NyBoard Bittle is 'discontinued,' superseded by 'Bittle X' — the lineage continues but the specific funded product does not remain the actively-marketed item. (6) Cross-candidate hobbyist-feasibility claims hold up as broadly true (all three physically-inspected candidates remain genuinely buildable) but independent reviews and issue trackers (Gadgeteer, Tom's Hardware, Hackaday.io Sawppy build logs, LeRobot GitHub issues) consistently report friction, tool prerequisites, and cost overruns understated by the brief's largely vendor/press-sourced framing. No target claim was found unfalsifiable or unworkable as scoped; all search angles in the plan were executable.
